info.desc: Last Splash is the second album by alternative rock band The Breeders, released in August 1993. Pixies bassist Kim Deal formed the band as a side project. Last Splash was the band's most successful album, certified Platinum by the RIAA for selling more than one million copies. The title of the album is taken from a lyric of its lead single, "Cannonball". This single has been used in many movie trailers, including Dude, Where's My Car? and South Park. A looped guitar sample of the song "S.O.S." was used by The Prodigy in their 1996 hit single "Firestarter". .

podcast.body: Released in August 1993, this album "exploded" in popularity, largely due to the success of its single, "Cannonball." "In August 1993, a record called Last Splash. This thing exploded, thanks mainly to a single called Cannonball."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The band's second album, released at the end of August 1993, achieved massive success, reportedly selling more copies than all of The Pixies' records combined up to that point. It became a significant alt-rock hit in North America and was particularly popular in the UK and, notably, France. "The second album came out at the end of August of 1993 and it blew up. I think this album sold more copies that all of the Pixies records put together to that point."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
